bugs.what: At the barrow's throne room, choosing 'weigh what each choice would mean' before deciding, or the gray priest's blessing, could become moot: after using the hunter's secret gap to enter the barrow (bypassing the sealed doors), returning to the priest for 'a blessing for the barrow' produced a dead-end line ('the doors are already open... say the words yourself') with no mechanical effect, even though the reeve/priest door-sealing questline implied the blessing mattered. Minor narrative dead branch, not blocking.
bugs.where: Gray Chapel / priest 'a blessing for the barrow'

bugs.what: Retrying a failed skill check (e.g. dragging the skiff free, pressing Aldous, settling the door, searching hearing rolls) raises the DC each time, which is well-telegraphed, but there's no way to see the cap ('stops at 20/23/27') until after several fails; a single upfront mention of the scaling rule would help players decide whether to keep retrying.

Companion party-dispute 'settle it' diplomacy checks (will, DC 11, decent modifiers) failed 3 of 5 times I attempted them, each failure dropping regard with two companions simultaneously; given these appear right after major grief-resolution beats, a bad roll can feel punishing relative to the effort spent optimizing that resolution.

confusions: It's not obvious up front that party regard, standing with factions, and holds rested all interact with the eventual ending gating (3 hollows rested + king rested + confession) — this only becomes clear via the status command, which the tutorial mentions but doesn't emphasize as essential reading.

Crossing the Pass Gate into Marrowgate is flagged as 'final' for unfinished threads, but many still-open side quests (Vane's road, Perrin's mother, Prior's Trust, etc.) don't clearly state ahead of time which specific ones would become permanently unresolvable vs. which might still resolve via later game text.

The 'name it' peaceful pacify option for hostile guardians (wight, honour guard, pilgrim) isn't hinted at contextually before first use — I found it by scrolling to 'more in this room,' and a first-time player relying only on visible top options might default to combat.
suggestions: Surface the party-heal-at-hearth mechanic and 'rest' locations more proactively in early hints, since it's easy to enter high-stakes fights (like the honour guard) with a wounded party and no idea a nearby rest point exists.
Give a one-line warning the first time a forced-try check's DC has scaled past a threshold, so players know when to stop retrying versus try a different approach.

Consider surfacing peaceful/pacify options (like 'name it') on the first page of a hostile-encounter menu rather than requiring 'more in this room' to discover them, especially for a Scholar-type build where lore-based pacification is the class fantasy.
A short reminder near Coldpass that companions' own personal arcs (not just generic side quests) get locked out permanently would help players prioritize which loose threads to tie up first.
